Is the expectation that the output will have the original dtypes, i.e. `int64, Int64, int64` ?

> Is the expectation that the output will have the original dtypes, i.e. `int64, Int64, int64` ?

for the code sample, that would be reasonable, although returning `float64` for the `Int64` columns would probably also be acceptable as that was the return type before the regression.

How does the changes in PR relate to the changes in the PR that caused the regression #41706? (or to put it a different way, which change in #41706 caused the regression and how does this PR rectify that?)

Before https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/pull/41706, the actual calculation was happening in `agg_general` in `result = self.aggregate(lambda x: npfunc(x, axis=self.axis))`.
Honestly, I didn't try to undo what that patch did, I went on to fix the inconsistency in the result coming post that patch.

Agreed @debnathshoham - on master, the dtypes in @simonjayhawkins' example come out at all float. What you have here is certainly an improvement over that, but it doesn't fully fix the regression. It's unclear to me if this patch is a good step in fully resolving the regression, or if fully solving it would make this patch obsolete. Will need to investigate more.

Thanks @debnathshoham for all the effort here. I apologize that I've not looked in detail at the fix but a regression fix should probably not need so much new logic added. I could be wrong though!

1.3.3 is scheduled for tomorrow. moving to 1.3.4 to allow more time for discussion.

Trying to explain what changed in #41706, and how I tried to remediate that (I am sure there will be more elegant / better way to do this).

**Previous Behavious**
There are multiple funcs (e.g. `sum`, `var`) that rely on `_cython_agg_general` for calculation, and for `axis=1` with `mixed` it is transposed and hence is cast to `object` (xref #43337). But I think that might be the expected behaviour (mentioned under `Notes` in [docs](https://pandas.pydata.org/pandas-docs/dev/reference/api/pandas.DataFrame.transpose.html)).

Since `numeric_only` is `True`, these data s dropped.
Before #41706, this used to raise `DataError` and was handled separately in `_agg_general`. (But  this didn't cover all the cases and raised incorrectly in some. I have seen `groupby.std` and `groupby.var` but could be others).

Since this error was removed in that PR, it was returning empty dataframe silently.

**This PR**
I have firstly tried to cast the transposed dataframe to the `common_dtype`, so we get the correct result first. Then I tried to cast it back to the original dtypes in `_maybe_recast_columns_if_transposed`. So there can be a few cases where the dtype of result and input will differ (like in `std`/`var` where they mostly become floating).

I tried to look for a function to cast a dataframe to certain dtypes, and if not possible upcast (say int -> float, Int -> Float). Unfortunately I was not able to find that. So i tried to match the values of post_cast vs. pre_cast to check if something is truncated. If something is truncated, I returned the previous result w/o casting, otherwise cast it to match the input dtypes.

Hope this helps.

I another simple, alternative would be to amend `numeric_only` to account for the transpose and subsequent object casting (this may be better as well, but this won't exactly match `1.2.5`).
i think let's try just reverting https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/pull/41706 instead of trying to fix this. (and then deprecate what is needed instead)

Doesn't the PR that changes DataFrame.transpose fix this?  That seems like a much better option than reverting #41706, which fixed a bunch of bugs.

Again shout it from the rooftops: this is caused by the lack of 2D EAs.

issue_context.title: BUG: groupby aggregation methods produce empty DataFrame with mixed DataTypes
issue_context.body:
- [x ] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.

- [x ] I have confirmed this bug exists on the latest version of pandas.

- [ ] (optional) I have confirmed this bug exists on the master branch of pandas.

---

**Note**: Please read [this guide](https://matthewrocklin.com/blog/work/2018/02/28/minimal-bug-reports) detailing how to provide the necessary information for us to reproduce your bug.

#### Code Sample, a copy-pastable example

```python
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame([[1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]]*3)
df.columns = pd.MultiIndex.from_product([['a', 'b'], ['i', 'j', 'k']])

print('all normal int:')
print(df.groupby(level=1, axis=1).sum())

for col in df.columns:
    if col[-1] == 'j':
        df[col] = df[col].astype('Int64')

print('mixed int:')
print(df.groupby(level=1, axis=1).sum())

for col in df.columns:
    df[col] = df[col].astype('Int64')

print('all nullable int:')
print(df.groupby(level=1, axis=1).sum())

```

#### Problem description

If columns have mixed datatypes, in the example partially normal ints and partially nullable ints, several aggregation methods in the example .sum(), of the DataFrameGroupBy objects unexpectedly return empty DataFrames. This behavior was not yet present in version 1.2.5.

#### Expected Output

Output should be the same for mixed and non mixed
